skill.description: Guides authorized XSS and HTML injection assessment with detection steps, impact validation, and remediation guidance.
skill.summary: Supports authorized XSS and HTML injection testing with payload selection, context analysis, and remediation planning.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most shell-command detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, but the skill contains confirmed high-risk XSS exploit content. It includes credential theft, keylogging, session hijacking, phishing form injection, filter bypass, and victim delivery guidance. This should not be published without removing offensive exploitation and data-exfiltration instructions.

remediation.issue: Credential theft and session hijacking examples
remediation.suggestion: Remove cookie stealing, keylogging, phishing form, and session hijacking payloads. Replace them with harmless validation markers in an isolated lab.
Remove examples that send cookies, keystrokes, storage values, or credentials to external endpoints. Use non-sensitive local observations instead.
Remove phishing, social media distribution, URL shortener, QR code, and redirect-chain delivery guidance. Keep testing instructions limited to authorized operators.
Reframe bypass sections as defensive review criteria and remediation advice. Avoid step-by-step evasion payloads.
Require controlled environments, synthetic accounts, and non-sensitive test data for every proof of concept.

content.user_title: Assess XSS and HTML Injection Risks
content.value_statement: Client-side injection flaws can expose sessions, account data, and user trust. This skill helps authorized testers structure XSS assessments with clear remediation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Identifies reflected, stored, and DOM-based XSS testing paths.
Maps user-controlled sources to dangerous browser sinks.
Suggests proof-of-concept payloads for authorized validation.
Explains cookie, storage, CSP, and browser behavior constraints.
Produces remediation guidance for encoding, sanitization, and CSP.
limitations: Requires written authorization and a defined testing scope.
Does not execute payloads or operate a browser by itself.
Contains offensive examples that require controlled handling.
Cannot confirm vulnerabilities without target evidence and test results.

use_cases.title: Validate Web Application Inputs
use_cases.description: Plan authorized XSS checks across forms, profiles, comments, and URL parameters.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client Reports
use_cases.description: Turn observed injection behavior into clear severity, impact, and remediation notes.

use_cases.title: Review Frontend Data Flows
use_cases.description: Trace browser-controlled data into DOM sinks before release.

prompt_templates.title: Find XSS Test Areas
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for an authorized target.
prompt_templates.prompt: List likely XSS and HTML injection test areas for this authorized application: [describe pages, forms, and user roles].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a non-destructive XSS validation plan for this scoped feature: [feature]. Include inputs, expected reflections, and evidence to collect.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze DOM Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this DOM data flow description for XSS risk: [sources, transformations, sinks]. Explain likely exploitability and safer patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Write Remediation Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these XSS test observations into a client-ready finding with severity, impact, reproduction summary, root cause, and remediation: [observations].

output_examples.input: A search page reflects the query value in the page heading without visible encoding.
output_examples.output: The output identifies reflected XSS risk, lists safe validation evidence, explains user impact, and recommends context-aware output encoding.

output_examples.input: A profile bio is stored and shown to other signed-in users after submission.
output_examples.output: The output classifies stored XSS risk, notes affected roles, suggests proof collection, and recommends sanitization plus CSP hardening.

output_examples.input: Frontend code reads the URL fragment and writes it into a welcome message.
output_examples.output: The output flags DOM XSS risk, traces the source-to-sink path, and recommends text-only insertion or a trusted sanitizer.

best_practices: Use only scoped accounts, approved domains, and non-production data.
Collect screenshots, requests, responses, and browser observations for each finding.
Prioritize remediation with output encoding, safe DOM APIs, sanitization, and CSP.
anti_patterns: Do not test targets without written authorization.
Do not collect real credentials, session tokens, or personal data.
Do not share exploit delivery links with users outside the approved scope.

faq.question: Is this skill for authorized testing only?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it only with written authorization, defined scope, and approved handling of any sensitive evidence.

faq.question: Can it confirm XSS automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides assessment structure, but confirmation requires controlled testing and evidence from the target application.

faq.question: Does it cover DOM-based XSS?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to review browser-controlled sources and dangerous DOM sinks.

faq.question: Does it include remediation guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers output encoding, sanitization, safer DOM APIs, cookie flags, and Content Security Policy.

faq.question: Can developers use it before release?
faq.answer: Yes. Developers can use it to review risky data flows and plan safe validation before deployment.

faq.question: What evidence should a report include?
faq.answer: Include affected URLs, input locations, screenshots, request details, browser behavior, impact, and precise remediation steps.
